pick.headline: Sakharov exiled to Gorky
pick.summary: On January 22, 1980, the dissident physicist Andrei Sakharov was detained in Moscow and sent into internal exile in the closed city of Gorky.
pick.significance: His banishment, weeks after the Afghanistan invasion, symbolized the Brezhnev regime's crackdown on dissent. Gorbachev released him in December 1986.
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of January 22, 1980, listed, in its contents under National Affairs, a "Late Report: Sakharov Deprived of Titles, Arrest Rumored", among routine Supreme Soviet election and personnel items.
